To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the DENV3 NS5 protein provides direct evidence for the flexibility of NS5 that may be required to perform its enzymatic functions, and that the inter-domain interface is important for NS5 function and virus replication.

the full-length NS protein from dengue virus serotype-3 adopts an ordered conformation with a well-ordered inter-domain linker region and a polar interface between the methyltransferase and polymerase domains, which are both important for virus replication.
the crystal structure of the dengue virus NS5 protein reveals a novel inter-domain interface that is essential for NS5 flexibility and virus replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of flavivirus replication.
the molecular basis of RNA replication by the NS5 protein of the dengue virus.
the structural biology of flavivirus replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NS5 structure is a dynamic protein, which has been demonstrated by the crystal structure, solution studies (HDX- and NMR) and the functional studies.
the structure of the full length dengue virus NS5 protein reveals a novel inter-domain interface essential for protein flexibility and virus replication.
NS5 from DENGUE V3 is a novel inter-domain interface essential for protein flexibility and virus replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NS5 protein from DENV3 adopts a novel conformation in which the MTase and the RdRp domains are oriented differently from the JEV NS5 structure.

the crystal structure of the DENV3 NS5 protein reveals a novel interface between the MT and RdRp domains that is essential for protein flexibility and virus replication, and that the interface may represent a new target for anti-flavivirus therapeutics.

the crystal structure and solution studies of the full length DENV3 NS5 protein reveal a novel interface between the N-terminal MTase and C-terminal RdRp domains, and that this interface is essential for the function of NS5 in virus replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of full-length DENV NS5 reveals an ordered inter-domain interface that is essential for protein flexibility and for viral replication.

the structure of NS5 from a dengue serotype 3 virus (DENV3), determined at 2.3 angstroms in the presence of SAH and GMP, shows that the inter-domain interface of this protein is highly conserved across flaviviruses.
NS5 is a flexible protein that can assume a variety of conformations, and this flexibility is likely to be important for the function of the protein in virus replication.
